name: Sample NBFC policy for small-business term loans (made up for this demo)
note: Every rule and number here is invented for a demo. It is not any real lender's policy.

rules.text: The business must have been operating for at least 3 years.
The promoter's credit bureau score must be at least 700.
No loan repayment may have been more than 30 days late in the last 12 months.
DSCR (yearly cash profit divided by yearly loan repayments, including the new loan) must be at least 1.25.
Total debt, including the new loan, must not exceed 3.5 times yearly cash profit (EBITDA).
Current ratio (short-term assets divided by short-term liabilities) must be at least 1.2.
Sales reported in GST returns must be within 10% of revenue in the audited financials.
Money received in the bank must be at least 80% of GST-reported sales.
No more than 1 bounced cheque or EMI in the last 6 months.
All required documents must be present: KYC, bureau report, audited financials for 2 years, 12 months of GST returns and 12 months of bank statements.
